references.text: The Mosaic law allowed picking grain by hand when walking through another person's field, which the disciples did here.
The Sabbath commandment in the Ten Commandments, which the Pharisees believed the disciples broke by picking grain on the Sabbath.
The parallel passage in Matthew that tells of the same event where the disciples picked grain on the Sabbath.
The parallel passage in Mark that tells of the same event where the disciples picked grain on the Sabbath.
The Sabbath commandment repeated in Deuteronomy, which forms the background for the conflict over what is allowed on the Sabbath.
Jesus declares himself Lord of the Sabbath, which is the conclusion of this event and explains his attitude toward Sabbath rules.
Another Sabbath conflict in Luke where Jesus challenges the Pharisees' interpretation of the Sabbath commandment.
Yet another Sabbath conflict in Luke that shows Jesus' consistent attitude toward the Sabbath and human needs.
